paper.title: The multi-armed bandit problem with covariates

settings.definition_quote: Let $\cI=\{1,\ldots, K+1\}$ be a given set of $K+1 \ge2$ arms. Successive pulls of arm $i \in\cI$ yield rewards $Y_1^{(i)}, Y_2^{(i)}, \ldots$ that are i.i.d. random variables in $[0,1]$ with expectation given by $\E[Y_t^{(i)}] = f^{(i)}\in[0,1]$. ... we further assume that the best arm is \textit{unique}

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed nonparametric bandit with covariates, class M_X^K(alpha, beta, L)
unmapped: i.i.d. covariates X_t in [0,1]^d with density bounded above and below
mean reward functions f^(i)(x) are (beta, L)-Hölder with beta in (0,1]
margin condition with parameter alpha: P_X[0 < f* - f# <= delta] <= C_0 delta^alpha for delta <= delta_0
learner knows Hölder exponent beta (and L for ABSE); does not need alpha
regret measured against the oracle policy pulling argmax_i f^(i)(X_t) at each round
settings.definition_quote: We denote by $\cM_{\cX}^K(\alpha,\beta,L)$ the class of $K$-armed bandit problems with covariates in $\cX=[0,1]^d$ with a machine satisfying the margin condition with parameter $\alpha>0$, the smoothness condition with parameters $(\beta,L)$ and such that $P_X$ has a density, with respect to the Lebesgue measure, bounded above and below

source.label: THstatic
source.quote: Consider a $(K+1)$-armed bandit problem where horizon is a random variable $N$ of expectation $n$ that is independent of the random rewards. When implemented with parameters $T, \gamma\geq1$, the \textsc{se} policy $\hpi$ exhibits an expected regret bounded, for any $\Delta\ge0$, as \E[R_N(\hpi)]\leq392 \gamma^2 (1+\frac{n}{T})\frac{K}{\Delta}\blog(\frac{T\Delta^2}{18\gamma^2}) + n \Delta^-

results.notes: blog(x)=max(log x,1). Regret defined via means, so pseudo-regret. The policy does not need n; T is a tuning parameter.

symbols.K_s: paper's K: number of suboptimal arms
symbols.K_0: any integer K_0 <= K_s (gaps sorted decreasingly)
symbols.Delta_K0: gap of arm K_0 (gaps sorted Delta_1 >= ... >= Delta_K)

conditions: horizon random N with expectation n

source.label: CorStatic
source.quote: Under the setup of Theorem~\ref{THstatic}, the \textsc{se} policy $\hpi$ run with parameter $T=n$ and $\gamma=1$ satisfies for any $K_0 \leq K$, \E R_N(\hpi)\leq646\sum_{i=1}^{K_0} \frac{\blog(n\Delta^2_{i} )}{\Delta_{i}}+304\frac{K-K_0}{\Delta_{K_0}}\blog(n\Delta^2_{K_0})+n\Delta_{K_0+1}.

results.notes: Gaps indexed in decreasing order; arms sorted with Delta_1 >= ... >= Delta_K.

conditions: horizon random N with expectation n

conditions: horizon random N with expectation n

tuning: M = floor((n/(K log K))^(1/(2 beta + d)))
SE in each bin with T = n M^{-d}, gamma = 1

source.label: THmain
source.quote: Fix $\beta\in(0,1]$, $L>0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and consider a problem in $\cM^K_{\cX}(\alpha,\beta,L)$. Then the \textsc{bse} policy $\bpi$ with $M=\lfloor(\frac{n}{K\log(K)} )^{1/(2\beta+d)}\rfloor$ has an expected regret at time $n$ bounded as follows: \E R_n(\bpi)\le C n (\frac{K\log K}{n})^{{\beta(\alpha+1)}/({2\beta+d})}, where $C>0$ is a positive constant that does not depend on $K$.

results.notes: Constant C does not depend on K but depends on other problem constants.

tuning: SE in each bin with T = n|B|^d, gamma = 2
k_0 smallest integer with 2^{-k_0} <= (K log K / n)^{1/(d+2beta)}

source.label: THmainadap
source.quote: Fix $\beta\in(0,1]$, $L>0$, $\alpha>0$, assume that $n \ge K\log(K)$ and consider a problem in $\cM^K_{\cX}(\alpha,\beta,L)$. If $\alpha<\infty$, then the \textsc{abse} policy $\tpi$ has an expected regret at time $n$ bounded by \E R_n(\tpi)\le C n (\frac{K\log(K)}{n})^{{\beta(\alpha+1)}/({2\beta+d})}, where $C>0$ does not depend on $K$. If $\alpha=\infty$, then $\E R_n(\tpi)\le C K\log(n)$.

results.notes: Minimax optimal for K=2 by cited lower bounds. ABSE does not need alpha.

conditions: alpha = infinity (one arm optimal everywhere, others bounded away)
tuning: SE in each bin with T = n|B|^d, gamma = 2
results.notes: Constant C may depend on problem constants (e.g. gap lower bound) but not K.
